components.name: base_humanoid
components.description:
Generic humanoid body for simulation agents. Provides a minimal but
functional set of sensors and affordances that let the agent physically
interact with its environment. This is the default embodiment for sim mode.

components.name: host_machine
components.description:
Production host machine — the physical or virtual server running the
agent. Scene entity (not self) with read-only sensors fed by system
monitoring. No callable affordances — the agent observes its host but
does not control hardware via SEM. Hardware-control actions (restart
service, clear cache) stay in the tool registry where autonomy gating
is mature.

components.name: infant_humanoid
components.description:
Infant humanoid body for the cradle sensorimotor development scenario.
Extends base_humanoid with interoceptive drives (hunger, thirst,
core temperature) and somatosensory sub-sensors (thermal, pressure,
texture) on arms and head. Drives use the homeostatic/entropic
protocol for biologically-grounded need signals.

components.name: infant_humanoid_chilled
components.description:
Exp 42 body (docs/experiments/42_substrate_primary_preference.md). Two
changes vs the shared infant_humanoid:

(1) An ENTROPIC `cold` drive — it rises over time (like hunger) and is
relieved by a warmth source's warm_self (self_effect cold: -0.3). Entropic
(not homeostatic) is load-bearing: a homeostatic cold drifts toward comfort
and SATIATES after a few warms, so warming stops and the exploitation-phase
metric floors (the Exp 41 trap). An entropic cold REGENERATES → warming
recurs → many exploitation warm-choices. The affinity table maps
cold -> (warm, fire, blanket, huddle), so the raw `cold` value drives
warm-tool selection directly (no homeostatic-deficit derivation needed).

(2) hunger/thirst kept but RATE-LIMITED: their drift_rate is low enough that
their value stays < 0.5 across the run, so they never enter the substrate's
drive-affinity selection competition (gate is drive_value > 0.5) and warming
dominates. deprivation_pain also lowered for a clean pain cascade. The
depletion *rate*, not the valence, is what removes the competition.

Distinct entity.name (avoids the all-components-into-one-registry tool-name
collision). Shared infant_humanoid and Exp 41's infant_humanoid_cold are
left untouched.

components.name: infant_humanoid_cold
components.description:
Cold variant of infant_humanoid for the Exp 41 substrate-primary
counter-prior experiment (docs/plans/archive/substrate_exploration_policy.md /
docs/experiments/41_substrate_primary_exploration.md). It starts and
STAYS cold — core_temperature well below set_point with a slow warm-back
drift — so warmth-seeking is a SUSTAINED, drive-relevant temptation. The
substrate's drive-affinity heuristic (via the derived "cold" need in
runtime/agent_loop._read_drive_states) then surfaces the deceptive
hearth's warm_self as a high-value action; the experiment measures whether
the agent learns to AVOID it despite the cold pull, because warm_self
breaches the arms' thermal comfort band (pain).

Deliberately a SEPARATE body so the shared infant_humanoid (Exp 37/38
LLM-AUT calibration: initial -0.15, comfort_band 0.25, pain_scale 1.5)
is untouched. entity.name is inherited from the parent (infant_humanoid)
so tool names stay identical to a normal cradle run.

components.name: infant_humanoid_naming_v1
components.description:
Roy-5b cradle priming body. Extends bodies/infant_humanoid
unchanged (drives, sub-sensors, modulators) and adds the
naming_events metadata that the EmbodimentPerceptSource consumes
to deterministically emit interoceptive vocalizations ("hungry",
"thirsty", "warm") when drives cross threshold.

Extending bodies/infant_humanoid (not bodies/base_humanoid)
inherits drive thresholds + drift rates from the canonical
cradle body, so future drift-curve tuning on infant_humanoid
propagates here and the "single-variable change vs Roy-4"
promise in the spec doc holds.

This body is research scaffolding for the Roy-5b iteration only —
production cradle sims keep bodies/infant_humanoid. See
docs/plans/archive/roy_5_encoder_alignment_disambiguator.md Stage 3 +
src/maxim/embodiment/naming_events.py.

components.name: infant_operant
components.description:
Infant body for the cradle_mother OPERANT orient experiment. Identical to
infant_humanoid EXCEPT the inherited azimuth centeredness drive is REMOVED
(drive: null). Rationale (2026-07-21 design pass): probes 1/2 proved the
intrinsic centeredness drive teaches orienting ALL BY ITSELF — an infant
with that drive orients whether or not a mother is present, which confounds
the "raised by a mother" claim. With the drive gone, turning relieves
nothing intrinsically; the infant perceives direction (the azimuth sensor
stays) but has no innate reason to orient. Its ONLY reward for orienting is
the mother's contingent feeding via NAc.credit_operant_reward — so orienting
is LEARNED from her, not innate (run with MAXIM_OPERANT_ONLY_CREDIT=1 so the
tool-success floor doesn't drown the operant signal — see probe 3).

components.name: infant_operant_satiated
components.description:
Exp 52 (Nurture) control body: identical to infant_operant — no intrinsic
orient drive, azimuth sensor kept — but NEVER HUNGRY. Hunger and thirst start
at 0 and do not drift, so the mother's contingent feed relieves nothing and,
under relief-sourced operant credit (reactive_mother_tick credit="relief"),
mints NO reward. Same feed events, same contingency, zero need: if this arm
learns to orient, the credit is not coming from relief. This is the arm that
separates "learns to want" from "learns to be fed"
(docs/experiments/protocols/exp52_nurture_preregistration.md).

components.name: reachy_mini
components.description:
SEM template for the Reachy Mini robot — the desktop humanoid head from Pollen
Robotics that started Maxim's embodiment journey. This template models the
robot's joints, cameras, microphones, and antennas as SEM entities so the
cognitive stack can reason about its own body.

Drop this into a campaign or simulation to give the agent a Reachy-shaped
body without needing the actual hardware connected. The same shape works
against the simulated controller.

components.name: cradle_blanket
components.description:
A soft warm blanket. Acquirable — picking it up adds its thermal
warmth (+0.2) to the agent's sensor space. When the agent is cool
(below core temperature set_point), this provides homeostatic
relief. When warm, it adds discomfort. Contextual valence from
the homeostatic drive protocol.

components.name: cradle_button
components.description:
A button that produces a pleasant chime when pressed. Provides
positive sensory feedback without physical consequences.

components.name: cradle_cool_air
components.description:
A persistent cool draft in the cradle room. Non-acquirable ambient
entity. Touching it (standing in the draft) cools the agent's
core temperature and arm thermal sensors. The agent must learn
to use the blanket to counteract the cooling and reach homeostasis.

components.name: cradle_false_hearth
components.description:
A small hearth that radiates heat. Non-acquirable — the agent
cannot pick it up. Proximity effects are handled by orchestrator
sensor writes to the agent's thermal sensors. The thermal-contact
reflex provides the narrative fallback layer.

components.name: cradle_fire_pit
components.description:
A small fire pit that radiates heat. Non-acquirable — the agent
cannot pick it up. Proximity effects are handled by orchestrator
sensor writes to the agent's thermal sensors. The fire_burn reflex
provides the narrative fallback layer.

components.name: cradle_food
components.description:
A food source with multiple portions. Eating reduces the agent's
hunger via self_effect. Portions decrease on consumption.

components.name: cradle_lever_door
components.description:
A lever mechanism connected to a door. Pulling the lever opens
the door, revealing food behind it. The orchestrator handles the
narrative consequence (auto-sense picks up newly visible entities).

components.name: cradle_sharp_rock
components.description:
A sharp rock that causes laceration when grasped. Acquirable —
picking it up reparents it to the agent's body and its sharpness
sensor joins the damage model (contact sensation layer).

components.name: warmth_alpha_harm
components.description:
Generic warmth source — identity ALPHA, HARMFUL variant (Exp 42,
docs/experiments/42_substrate_primary_preference.md). warm_self relieves
the entropic `cold` drive BUT breaches the arms' thermal comfort band
(arms.thermal +0.6 > band 0.5) → thermal_contact pain → negative causal
link. Identical to warmth_alpha_safe except the arms.thermal delta.

components.name: warmth_alpha_safe
components.description:
Generic warmth source — identity ALPHA, SAFE variant (Exp 42 counter-
balanced preference experiment, docs/experiments/42_substrate_primary_preference.md).
warm_self relieves the entropic `cold` drive without breaching the arms'
thermal comfort band — no pain, so it accrues a positive/neutral causal
link. Symmetric with warmth_beta_*; the only systematic difference from
warmth_alpha_harm is the arms.thermal delta.

components.description:
